description: EtcdBackupPolicy takes encrypted etcd snapshots of one TalosCluster on a schedule and keeps a bounded number of them. Each snapshot is recorded as an EtcdSnapshot. Taking a snapshot reads etcd and changes no machine, so it needs no approval; restoring one does (docs site: operate/day-2/restore-etcd).

fields.name: spec
fields.description: EtcdBackupPolicySpec says how often to snapshot one cluster's etcd, how long to keep the snapshots, where to keep them and whom to encrypt them for.

fields.name: clusterRef
fields.description: ClusterRef names the TalosCluster whose etcd is backed up.

validations.message: clusterRef is frozen: create another policy for another cluster

fields.name: encryption
fields.description: Encryption names who can read the snapshots.

fields.name: ageRecipients
fields.description: AgeRecipients are age public keys (age1..., from age-keygen -y). Any one of their identities decrypts a snapshot; the operator holds none, so it cannot. Name at least two people or a person and a key kept offline, so that a restore does not hang on one key. Post-quantum keys (age1pq1...) cannot be mixed with classic ones.

fields.name: interval
fields.description: Interval is the time between scheduled snapshots (6h, 30m). At least 5m: a snapshot reads the whole database from one member.

fields.name: retention
fields.description: Retention bounds how many snapshots are kept, and for how long.

fields.name: count
fields.description: Count is how many verified snapshots to keep, the newest.

fields.name: maxAge
fields.description: MaxAge deletes verified snapshots older than this (168h for a week). Unset keeps any age, up to Count.

fields.name: sink
fields.description: Sink is where the encrypted snapshots are stored.

validations.message: set exactly one of s3 or pvc

fields.name: pvc
fields.description: PVC stores snapshots on the operator's backup volume (the config/etcd-backup component mounts a PersistentVolumeClaim into the manager). Refused for the cluster the operator itself runs on: that volume lives on the etcd it would back up, and is lost with it.

fields.name: s3
fields.description: S3 stores snapshots in a bucket of an S3-compatible object store, off the cluster: the sink for production.

validations.message: endpoint must be https://; set allowPlainHTTP: true only for a lab store, because http:// sends the store's credentials in the clear

fields.name: allowPlainHTTP
fields.description: AllowPlainHTTP lets endpoint be http://, for a store in a lab. The snapshots are encrypted either way, but the store's credentials and the snapshot keys are not, and anyone on the path can delete or replace the ciphertext. Never set it in production.

fields.name: bucket
fields.description: Bucket must exist; the operator does not create it.

fields.name: caSecretRef
fields.description: CASecretRef names a Secret in the operator's namespace whose key ca.crt (PEM) replaces the system roots for the endpoint.

fields.name: credentialsSecretRef
fields.description: CredentialsSecretRef names a Secret in the operator's namespace with keys accessKeyID and secretAccessKey. Give the key write, read, list and delete on the bucket (or the prefix) and nothing else.

fields.name: endpoint
fields.description: Endpoint is the store's URL, https://host[:port] (https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com, https://minio.example:9000). http:// needs allowPlainHTTP.

fields.name: pathStyle
fields.description: PathStyle sends requests as https://host/bucket/key, which most stores other than AWS need.

fields.name: prefix
fields.description: Prefix goes in front of every key; the key is <prefix><cluster>/<snapshot>.db.age.

fields.name: region
fields.description: Region of the bucket; empty lets the client ask the store.

fields.name: suspend
fields.description: Suspend stops scheduled snapshots; pk-metal backup now still takes one, and retention still prunes.

fields.name: status
fields.description: EtcdBackupPolicyStatus is the backup state of the cluster.

fields.name: conditions
fields.description: Conditions: Ready (the sink and recipients can be used) and BackedUp (a verified snapshot newer than twice the interval exists).

fields.name: lastTransitionTime
fields.description: lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed.  If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable.

fields.name: message
fields.description: message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string.

fields.name: observedGeneration
fields.description: observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown.

fields.name: type
fields.description: type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase.

fields.name: consecutiveFailures
fields.description: ConsecutiveFailures counts the snapshots that failed since the newest verified one.

fields.name: lastScheduleTime
fields.description: LastScheduleTime is when the last scheduled snapshot was started.

fields.name: lastSuccessfulSnapshot
fields.description: LastSuccessfulSnapshot is the newest verified snapshot.

fields.name: verifiedSnapshots
fields.description: VerifiedSnapshots counts the verified snapshots kept.
